note_fixes: Hebrews 12:23: replace the two-verse passage with 12:23 alone ('in joyful assembly, to the congregation of the firstborn, enrolled in heaven'); 12:22 is Mount Zion, the heavenly Jerusalem and the angels, which this concept does not need
concepts.why: Biblical-theological / secular scholar: the passage is longer than the concept needs, and 'joyful assembly' is the only part that touches praise in the assembly. Trim to 12:23. The other passages are sound; Ps 22:22 / Heb 2:12 are set side by side with no line between them.

Secular scholar / Baptist: Acts 20:20 is Paul teaching 'publicly and from house to house'. It does not say a church meets in a house, so it shares only the words 'house' and 'from house to house'. Acts 2:46 and 12:12 do show gatherings in homes and stay.

concepts.name: Those who call on the name
note_fixes: Romans 10:12: the verse says 'call on Him' and has no 'name'; Romans 10:13 ('everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved') is the verse that carries the phrase, so use 10:13 in its place
concepts.why: Jewish reader of the Hebrew Bible / secular scholar: 'the name of the LORD' (capitals, the divine name) is said by Gen 4:26, Zeph 3:9 and Joel 2:32 only. Acts 9:14, 1 Cor 1:2, Rom 10:12 and 2 Tim 2:22 say 'Your name', 'our Lord Jesus Christ', 'Him', 'the Lord'. A heading that says LORD over those four tells the reader the NT texts mean the LORD, and the texts leave that to the reader. 'Those who call on the name' fits all eight and keeps the texts' own words.

note_fixes: Hebrews 3:6: extend the note to 'But Christ is faithful as the Son over God's house. And we are His house, if we hold firmly to our confidence and the hope of which we boast' (exact, contiguous). The clipped note drops the 'if', which is the clause Reformed, Baptist and Wesleyan readers part over
concepts.why: Wesleyan (and Reformed / Baptist): a note that stops before 'if we hold firmly' hides the very clause on which readers disagree about perseverance. Clipping at that point reads as choosing the unconditional side. Quote it through.

Biblical-theological / Baptist / Reformed: 1 Peter 2:25 calls Christ 'the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls'. It names no church office, so it shares the word 'overseer' only. Also, Acts 20:17 (elders) and 20:28 (overseers) are one speech, and Titus 1:5 (elders) and 1:7 (overseer) are two verses of one passage. Putting each in a different concept hides the text's own adjacency from readers who hold the two words name one office; add a plain 'see also' each way between concepts 21 and 22, with no line on whether it is one office or two.

concepts.name: Keys, binding and loosing, forgiving sins
concepts.why: Baptist / Reformed / Catholic / Orthodox: only Matt 16:19 says 'keys'. Matt 18:18 (said to the disciples) and John 20:23 do not. 'The keys of the kingdom of heaven' as the heading says all three are the keys, which is a Lutheran and Catholic joining that other traditions reject. A name that lists what each passage says (keys; bind and loose; forgive and withhold) keeps the three side by side without saying they are one thing.

note_fixes: Acts 2:38: extend the note to 'Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins'. The clause 'for the forgiveness of your sins' is exactly where Lutheran, Catholic and Orthodox readers part from Baptist and Reformed ones; clipping it before the clause reads as a side

1 Peter 3:21: the note uses an ellipsis, so it is not an exact quotation, and the elided words ('not the removal of dirt from the body, but') are the half one side cites. Quote it contiguously: 'the baptism that now saves you also-not the removal of dirt from the body, but the pledge of a clear conscience toward God'. Also note that BSB 'this water symbolizes' renders Greek antitypon ('corresponding to'), which is a translator's reading; the original arbitrates
concepts.why: Lutheran / Catholic / Orthodox / Baptist: the label is plain and the passages are mostly well chosen, but two notes are cut exactly where traditions part. The set also lacks the texts that sacramental readers (Acts 22:16 'be baptized and wash away your sins', Gal 3:27, Col 2:12 'buried with Him in baptism') and Reformed household readers (Col 2:11-12) cite, while Acts 8:38, 2:41, 10:47 are all present; add Acts 22:16 and Col 2:12 (and optionally Gal 3:27) so the weight is even. Do not add a spirit-baptism text here; that is a separate missing sub-theme (see missing).

Secular scholar of the Hebrew (original arbitrates): Psalm 55:14's Hebrew is sod, 'intimate counsel' or 'sweet talk' with a friend (a betrayal psalm), not the Greek koinonia that 'the fellowship' names in Acts 2:42. 'Sweet fellowship' is the translator's word, so it shares a word with the concept only in English. The six NT passages are sound.

note_fixes: Galatians 3:28: the note uses an ellipsis, so it is not an exact quotation, and it silently removes 'slave nor free, male nor female', a clause on which readers part over women's place. Quote the whole verse: 'There is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male nor female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus', or drop Gal 3:28 from this concept (the verse is also better placed with the women-and-men sub-theme named under missing)
concepts.why: Secular scholar / Pentecostal / Wesleyan: a clipped note is an exact quotation of nothing, and cutting the male-and-female clause out of a verse readers argue over is a choice the site should not make for them. The rest of the concept (Isa 56:3, 57:19 beside Acts 2:39, 10:34-35, 15:9, Eph 2:13, 17) stands side by side with no line between.

Wesleyan / Reformed / Jewish reader, on Israel and the church: the set jumps from Rom 11:17-18 (grafted in) to 11:24 (natural branches grafted back), and leaves out the verse in between that is the dark half of the image: Rom 11:22 'severity to those who fell ... if you continue in His kindness. Otherwise, you also will be cut off.' Jer 11:16 keeps the fire in Israel's case; the same standard should keep the warning in the other. Add Rom 11:22 (or 11:20-22) so the image runs both ways as the text does.

Jewish reader / secular scholar: Isaiah 52:7 is good news told to Zion ('Your God reigns'), with no going out to the nations, so it does not say what 'Go and make disciples of all nations' says. Romans 10:15 already quotes the verse, so the pairing is still visible in the Romans verse itself, and nothing is lost by dropping the Isaiah passage here.

secondary_or_links: Secondary 'Greeting': add 'Church → Greeting with a holy kiss': Romans 16:16, 1 Corinthians 16:20, 2 Corinthians 13:12, 1 Peter 5:14. The texts name it four times; it is a plain practice with no side taken.

Secondary 'Laying on of hands': consider adding 2 Timothy 1:6 and Acts 8:17 beside Acts 6:6, 13:3, 1 Tim 4:14, so the set is not read only as commissioning or only as ordination; no comment either way.

Concept 25 (The breaking of bread) stands as drafted. For evenness of weight, consider adding 1 Corinthians 11:23-25 (Paul's account) and 11:27 ('guilty of sinning against the body and blood of the Lord') beside 10:16 and 11:26, which the Reformed, Catholic, Lutheran and Orthodox each cite; optional, not a fault.

Links: if the site has a theme on Israel or on the nations, link to it. Concepts 1, 6, 11, 21, 38, 39 and 41 carry Israel's passages and the olive tree, and the nine links as drafted do not include the theme that would hold them. Link to Worship and Prayer too if those themes exist (concepts 2, 27, 28).

missing.sub_theme: Expel the wicked man from among you
missing.why: The texts plainly develop the church putting a person out and then taking him back. The outline holds only 'tell it to the church' (Matt 18:17) and Titus 3:10 'reject a divisive man', so the discipline itself is missing, and it is the dark thread of this theme. 2 Cor 2:6-8 (restoration) is the other half. Needed so the theme does not soften itself.

missing.sub_theme: It seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us
missing.why: How the assembly decides. Acts 15:6 and 15:9 are used, but the decision itself ('the apostles and elders, with the whole church'; 'it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us') is not, nor Acts 6:2-5 ('the whole group ... chose'). Councils, congregations and elders each find their pattern here; the texts can stand side by side.

missing.sub_theme: The faith once for all delivered to the saints
missing.why: Keeping the teaching and testing teachers. 'Teaching' is only a secondary concept, and false teaching appears in one verse (Acts 20:29, the wolves). A reader of this theme expects the guarding of what was entrusted and the testing of spirits; the texts develop it across the letters.

missing.sub_theme: Women and men in the assembly
missing.why: A plain label. The outline treats offices and gifts but is silent on this, and every tradition's practice turns on these verses (Baptist, Pentecostal, Catholic, Orthodox, Wesleyan, Reformed and secular readers would all look for them). Leaving the section out is itself a side; set the texts that restrict and the texts that commend women's service side by side with no line between them. Gal 3:28 may be moved here from concept 38.

missing.sub_theme: All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit
missing.why: Acts opens the church with the Spirit's coming, yet no concept holds Pentecost or the later comings (in Acts 8, 10 and 19 the order of water, hands and Spirit differs; the texts stand side by side with no order claimed). Pentecostal and Charismatic readers would look for this first; it also keeps 1 Cor 12:13 from being the only place 'baptized' and 'Spirit' meet. Link to the Spirit theme as before.
